text_blocks.snippet: High blood pressure (hypertension) usually has no symptoms at all, which is why it is often called the "silent killer".
snippet_highlighted_words: usually has no symptoms at all

text_blocks.snippet: Most people can live with high blood pressure for years without knowing it. However, if blood pressure becomes dangerously high—known as severe hypertension or a hypertensive crisis (readings higher than 180/120 mm Hg)—a person may experience:

list.snippet: Vision changes (such as blurred or double vision)
Pounding in the chest, neck, or ears

text_blocks.snippet: If a blood pressure reading is higher than 180/120 mm Hg and accompanied by any of the following warning signs, it is a medical emergency:
Because symptoms are rare, the only reliable way to check for high blood pressure is through regular measurements at a doctor’s office or with an approved home monitor.
For official guidelines and reading categories, you can review the American Heart Association High Blood Pressure Guide or learn more via the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention.
